before.title: 1.2 PureTech Wet Timing Belt Degradation (Oil Contamination, Brake Assist Loss)
before.description: The 1.2 PureTech (EB2) three-cylinder petrol engine uses a timing belt that runs inside the engine oil ('wet belt'). The belt rubber degrades prematurely in aged or incorrect-spec oil, shedding particles that clog the oil pickup, oil ways and the brake vacuum pump, causing oil starvation, engine damage and loss of braking assistance. Stellantis launched UK safety recall R/2020/326 (campaign JZR) covering 22,580 vehicles including 3008 I and 3008 II built June 2013 to April 2017, and the wider belt problem on later builds has been handled through service actions and warranty extensions.
before.solution: Under recall/campaign JZR dealers update belt-wear detection software, inspect, and replace the timing belt and brake vacuum pump if contaminated; the sump and oil pickup should be cleaned of belt debris. Outside the recall, replace the wet belt early (around 6 years/60k miles rather than the original 10-year schedule) and use only the specified PSA B71 2010 0W-30 oil with shortened oil-change intervals.
symptoms: 'Engine fault: repair needed' warning on dash
Hard brake pedal / loss of brake assistance
Rough idle or misfires, loss of power
Low oil pressure warning light
Black rubbery sludge visible under the oil filler cap

before.title: 1.6 THP/VTi (Prince EP6) Timing Chain Stretch and Tensioner Failure
before.description: First-generation 3008s with the PSA/BMW Prince 1.6 petrol engines (turbo THP 156 and naturally aspirated VTi 120) suffer premature timing chain stretch caused by a soft original chain and a tensioner that is starved of oil, aggravated by the engine's aggressive variable valve timing. A stretched chain rattles on cold start and can jump or break, putting the engine out of synchronization and risking valve-to-piston contact and full engine failure. Peugeot issued revised chain and tensioner parts and a TSB, and forum-documented failures occurred well under 60,000 miles.
before.solution: Replace the timing chain kit (chain, tensioner, guides, sprockets) with the latest revised parts as soon as cold-start rattle or cam/crank correlation codes appear. Frequent oil changes with the correct grade slow chain wear; some owners obtained goodwill or warranty repairs from Peugeot UK under the in-force TSB.
symptoms: Metallic rattle from the engine on cold start
Engine management light with timing/synchronization fault
Rough running or loss of power
Engine cranks but won't start (chain jumped)
Whirring/grinding noise from the timing cover

before.title: BSI (Built-in Systems Interface) Module Faults Causing Erratic Electrics
before.description: The BSI module is the central body-electronics hub on the 3008 (BSI2010 on the Mk1, BSI EL3 on the Mk2), controlling the immobiliser, central locking, lighting, wipers and dash communication. Thermal cycling cracks its solder joints (particularly around the central-locking relay), and voltage instability from a weak battery or careless battery changes corrupts it, producing no-start conditions, immobiliser faults, hazard lights that won't cancel, bouncing door locks and random warning cascades. It is a long-documented Peugeot/Citroën weakness with an established independent repair industry around it.
before.solution: First perform the official BSI reboot/hard-reset procedure (controlled battery disconnect) and verify the battery and alternator are healthy, as voltage problems mimic BSI failure. Persistent faults are fixed by specialist BSI board repair (about $100–200) or a replacement unit coded to the car; many faults after battery changes clear with a dealer diagnostic reset.
symptoms: Car intermittently fails to start / immobiliser fault
Hazard or indicator lights flash and won't turn off
Central locking locks/unlocks by itself or 'bounces'
Wipers or lights operate erratically
Multiple random fault messages on the dash at once

before.title: HYbrid4 Diesel-Hybrid System and Battery Faults
before.description: The 2012–2016 3008 HYbrid4 (2.0 HDi diesel + rear electric motor) suffers hybrid-system faults from two sources: ageing of the Ni-MH high-voltage traction pack under the rear seats, whose poor ventilation accelerates cell imbalance, and an undersized 12V auxiliary battery whose low voltage triggers cascades of spurious fault messages and no-start conditions. Owners report 'Hybrid System Fault' and reduced-power warnings, loss of electric drive (and with it the car's all-wheel-drive capability), and rising fuel consumption when the electric side stops contributing.
before.solution: Always test and replace the 12V battery first, since many phantom hybrid faults disappear with a healthy auxiliary battery (a trickle charger helps cars used for short trips). Genuine HV pack failures are addressed with refurbished or repaired battery packs from hybrid specialists at a fraction of the new-unit price.
symptoms: 'Hybrid System Fault' or reduced power warning on dash
Electric drive / EV mode no longer engages
Noticeably higher fuel consumption
Car fails to start or shows random multiple warnings
4WD mode unavailable (rear axle is electric-only)

before.title: Rear Self-Levelling Hydraulic Suspension Leaks (3008 I, 2.0 HDi/HYbrid4)
before.description: First-generation 3008s fitted with the rear self-levelling hydraulic suspension (mainly 2.0 HDi 150 and HYbrid4 versions) commonly lose fluid from the crimped flexible pipe connections at the centre of the rear axle, with failures reported at as little as 30,000 miles. Once the fluid leaks out, the rear suspension knocks and crashes over bumps and the self-levelling function is lost, and the OEM hydraulic unit is expensive and prone to failing again.
before.solution: The accepted fix in the owner community is to remove the hydraulic self-levelling unit entirely and convert to conventional rear shock absorbers (the dampers from the 1.6 model are a direct fit), a roughly half-hour job that saves several hundred pounds over replacing the hydraulic system. Repairing the OEM unit is possible but rarely worthwhile.
symptoms: Knocking/banging from the rear over bumps
Oil visibly leaking around the centre of the rear axle
Rear ride height sags, especially when loaded
Bouncy, crashy rear ride quality
Hydraulic fluid film on rear suspension pipes

Do not buy a hydraulic unit, hose or conventional damper from this page; equipment, failure, load rating and fitment must be established first.
